hints: Look carefully at the wording. It asks for part of mitosis, not part of the whole cell cycle. Which of the three events sounds like a stage of nuclear division?
Remember the big picture: Cell cycle = interphase + mitosis (prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase) + cytokinesis. Which numbered event fits inside mitosis only?
walkthrough:
**Recall what the cell cycle includes**

Think of the cell cycle as the big umbrella. It has three main parts: interphase (growth and DNA replication), mitosis (nuclear division), and cytokinesis (splitting the cytoplasm).

So: $$\text{cell cycle = interphase + mitosis + cytokinesis}$$

**Check each listed event**

1 interphase is the long preparation stage before division, not part of mitosis. 2 metaphase is one of the four stages of mitosis, where chromosomes line up at the equator. 3 cytokinesis happens after mitosis to divide the cell in two, so it is separate from mitosis.

**Pick the mitosis-only event**

Only event 2 sits inside mitosis. That matches option D, 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect, as it includes interphase and cytokinesis which are separate stages of the cell cycle, not stages of mitosis.
options.B: Incorrect, as both interphase and cytokinesis occur outside mitosis, one before and one after nuclear division.
options.C: Incorrect, as interphase is the growth and DNA synthesis phase that prepares for mitosis but is not part of it.
options.D: Correct, as metaphase is a true stage of mitosis, along with prophase, anaphase and telophase.
